title: VANISHED | 19 Minutes: The Disappearance of Maura Murray
description:
February 9, 2004. A black car hits a snowbank on Route 112 in New Hampshire. A school bus driver stops to help. Nineteen minutes later, police arrive, and 21-year-old Maura Murray is gone. More than twenty years later, no trace of her has ever been found.

The fake email, the cash, the packed room, the scent that ended at the road, and the three main theories.

If you have any information, contact the New Hampshire State Police.

New real mystery every Wednesday and Saturday.

title: VANISHED | The Springfield Three: Gone From Their Own Home
description:
June 7, 1992. Springfield, Missouri. Sherrill Levitt and two 18 and 19-year-old graduates, Suzie Streeter and Stacy McCall, come home after a graduation night. By morning, all three are gone. Their cars are in the driveway. Their purses, keys and money are still inside. More than thirty years later, none of them has ever been found.

The broken porch light that was swept away, the obscene phone call, the erased answering-machine message, the hotline call that was cut off, and the parking garage nobody ever dug.

If you have any information, contact the Springfield Police Department.

New real mystery every Wednesday and Saturday.

description:

#shorts #history #sanfrancisco #pov #1906

Every fact is real: the SS Mont-Blanc burning in front of the city, the crew whose warning nobody could hear, the crowd watching from the shore and the windows, the explosion at 9:04 AM (2.9 kilotons, the largest human-made blast before the atomic age), the hundreds blinded by glass, the 60 foot wave, and the last telegraph message of train dispatcher Vince Coleman. 1,782 people died.

#shorts #history #halifax #pov #1917

You wake up in Johnstown, Pennsylvania, on May 31, 1889. It rained all night, and fourteen miles up the valley an old dam is holding back a lake.

Every fact is real: the private club that lowered the dam and never replaced its discharge pipes, the break just before 3 PM, the wall of water up to 60 feet high moving at 40 miles an hour, the 57 minutes it took to reach the town, the wreckage that piled up against the Stone Bridge and burned for three days, and the 2,208 dead. No club member was ever held legally responsible.

#shorts #history #johnstownflood #pov #1889

title: POV: You Wake Up in a Prison Cell in 1902. In One Minute, It Saves Your Life.
description:
You wake up in the dungeon of the prison of Saint-Pierre, Martinique, on May 8, 1902. At 8:02 AM, Mont Pelée erupts.

Every fact is real: two weeks of falling ash, the mudflow that buried about 150 people at the sugar works, the newspapers that said the city was safe, the glowing cloud hotter than 1,000 degrees that crossed the city in under a minute, and the roughly 28,000 dead. Ludger Sylbaris, locked in solitary confinement in a stone cell with one slit in the door, was found alive three days later. He was pardoned and toured with a circus as the man who lived through Doomsday.

#shorts #history #volcano #pov #1902
comment: The worst cell in the prison was the safest place in the city. Would you have believed the newspapers?

title: POV: You Wake Up in Siberia in 1908. The Sky Is About to Split in Two.
description:
You wake up at a trading post in Siberia on June 30, 1908. At 7:14 AM, something explodes over the forest of Tunguska.

Every fact is real: a witness about 40 miles away said the sky split in two, that his shirt felt like it was on fire, and that the blast threw him off his porch. About 830 square miles of forest were flattened, with an energy estimated between 3 and 50 megatons. For days the night sky glowed across Europe, bright enough to take photographs at midnight in Scotland and Sweden. The first expedition reached the center in 1927 and found no crater, only scorched trees still standing.

#shorts #history #tunguska #pov #mystery
comment: Run inside, or look at the sky. Be honest, which one would you have done?

title: POV: You Wake Up in Galveston in 1900. By Tonight, the Sea Takes the City.
description:
You wake up in Galveston, Texas, on September 8, 1900. By tonight, a hurricane will put the whole island under water.

Every fact is real: the island's highest point was 8.7 feet above the sea, the local Weather Bureau chief had written that a serious hurricane could not strike the city, and no seawall was built. Around 7:30 PM witnesses saw the water rise about four feet in four seconds, with winds measured at 100 mph. About 8,000 people died and 7,000 buildings were destroyed. It remains the deadliest natural disaster in U.S. history. Afterwards the city built a 17-foot seawall and raised its own ground level.

#shorts #history #hurricane #pov #1900
comment: Stay in your house, or wade to the brick buildings downtown. What would you have done?

You wake up in Chicago on October 8, 1871. Around 8:30 PM, a fire starts in a barn on DeKoven Street.

Every fact is real: one inch of rain in three months, a city of wooden houses with about 120 miles of wooden sidewalks, a watchman who sent the firemen to the wrong place, burning debris that carried the fire across the river twice, and the waterworks destroyed. About 17,500 buildings burned, 90,000 people lost their homes and around 300 died. The story that a cow kicked a lantern was printed right away. In 1893 the reporter admitted he had made it up.

#shorts #history #chicago #pov #1871

title: POV: You Wake Up in Murphysboro in 1925. The Deadliest Tornado in U.S. History Is Coming.
description:
You wake up in Murphysboro, Illinois, on March 18, 1925. Around 12:45 PM, a funnel touches down in Missouri.

Every fact is real: the Tri-State tornado crossed Missouri, Illinois and Indiana in about 3 hours and 45 minutes, on a path of 219 miles, moving at an average of 62 miles an hour and more than a mile wide. 695 people died, 234 of them in Murphysboro, and fires swept the ruins. It is still the deadliest tornado in American history. A baby carried about 1,200 yards from a farm was found uninjured.

#shorts #history #tornado #pov #1925

title: FEARS EXPLAINED | You Wake Up and Cannot Move. Something Is in the Room.
description:
Sleep paralysis, explained. You wake up, you are aware, and you cannot move or speak. Only your eyes still work.

Every fact is real: about 8% of people experience it at least once. It happens when waking and REM sleep overlap, so the mind is awake while the body is still in the paralysis of dreaming. The two classic hallucinations are the intruder, a presence or dark figure in the room, and the weight of something sitting on the chest. Episodes usually last one to six minutes, they are physically harmless, and sleeping on your back is one of the strongest triggers. The Old English word for the creature was mare, which is where nightmare comes from.

#shorts #horror #sleepparalysis #fear #scary
comment: Has this ever happened to you? What did you see in the room?

title: REAL HORROR | Three Girls Started Laughing in 1962. Then 1,000 People Could Not Stop.
description:
The Tanganyika laughter epidemic of 1962. It began on January 30 with three girls at a boarding school in Kashasha.

Every fact is real: 95 of the school's 159 students were affected and no teachers. Attacks of laughing and crying, with fainting, pain and rashes, lasted from a few hours to 16 days. The school closed on March 18, the girls went home, and it spread: 217 people in the village of Nshamba, 14 schools shut down and about 1,000 people affected. It faded 18 months after it started. Researchers explain it as mass psychogenic illness brought on by stress.

#shorts #horror #truestory #history #masshysteria
comment: Would you have stayed in that classroom? Be honest.

title: FEARS EXPLAINED | You Are Floating in the Open Ocean. Do Not Look Down.
description:
Thalassophobia, explained: the persistent, intense fear of deep bodies of water, and of what the depth could hold.

Every fact is real: the deep sea begins at about 200 meters, where the light starts to fade. At 1,000 meters the water is about 5 degrees Celsius. Pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 meters, passing 1,000 atmospheres in the deepest trenches. The Challenger Deep is 10,935 meters down, and as of July 2022 only 27 people had descended to it. Psychologists say fearing deep water makes evolutionary sense, and that we fear the dark because we cannot see.

#shorts #horror #thalassophobia #ocean #fear
comment: Could you float there without looking down? Be honest.

description:
Mattoon, Illinois, September 1944. A sweet smell in a bedroom, legs that would not move, and a tall man in dark clothes at the window. More than two dozen cases were reported in two weeks. Armed men patrolled the streets. A white cloth found on a porch was tested and no chemicals were found. The health commissioner said: "The whole town is sick with hysteria." No one was ever caught, and no one was seriously hurt.

#horror #truestory #history #mystery #shorts

title: FEARS EXPLAINED | Why an Almost Human Face Makes You Want to Run
description:
The uncanny valley. In 1970, robotics professor Masahiro Mori noticed that the more human a robot looks, the more we like it, until it looks almost human. Then the feeling turns to strong revulsion. One theory says the brain reads the face as a sign of disease or a corpse. Another says it reminds us of our own death. In a 2015 study, faces with the eyes removed felt more uncanny than faces with the nose removed.

#fear #uncannyvalley #psychology #horror #shorts

title: REAL HORROR | A Whole Town Ate the Same Bread. Then the Visions Began.
description:
Pont-Saint-Esprit, France, August 1951. More than 250 people fell ill after eating bread from the same bakery. Fifty were interned in asylums and seven died. Most researchers blame ergot poisoning; others point to mercury, and one 2009 book claims a CIA LSD test, a theory historians have heavily criticized.

description:

title: REAL HORROR | The Men Who Died in Their Sleep (The True Nightmare Behind Elm Street)
description:
Starting in the late 1970s, young and seemingly healthy Hmong refugee men in the United States began dying in their sleep, and doctors could not explain why. Years later, Wes Craven read small newspaper articles about men who died in the middle of nightmares, and turned them into A Nightmare on Elm Street.
